note: The one source for the seven Stack feature areas: the landing cards, the features index and every feature page come from this file. Every bullet was checked against the Stack code or docs on 2026-11-28; cut a bullet that cannot be shown. Each bullet is Shipped unless it says status.

areas.name: Setup
areas.card: Install and pick your hardware in minutes.
areas.lead: One installer and one admin page. Pick your computer's memory size and Stack suggests a setup that fits.

visual.alt: The AI and models page: one card per feature, and a Setup for this computer panel with the 16, 32, 64 and 128 GB setups.

bullets: Ready-made setups for 16, 32, 64 and 128 GB and up, matched to your computer's memory
Engines and models are pinned and checked against a checksum before they are used
Turn features on or off any time, on one page. A feature that is off uses no memory

areas.name: Memory and tiers
areas.card: Fit your hardware, protect your computer.
areas.lead: A memory guard loads only what fits, and a priority order keeps the work you need most loaded.

visual.alt: The Resources page: memory in use, how much of the engine budget is held, and memory by feature over time.

bullets: A ready-made setup for each memory size, with what stays loaded and what loads when asked
Four levels per feature, Reduced, Standard, Boost and Max, and you choose which model each level uses
A model that does not fit your memory is refused, with the reason in a sentence
A priority order, "Which feature goes first", decides who is served first when memory is tight
Engines that sit idle unload and free their memory

areas.name: The queue
areas.card: Run one job without slowing another.
areas.icon: <rect x="3" y="4" width="18" height="7" rx="2"/><rect x="3" y="13" width="18" height="7" rx="2"/><path d="M7 7.5h.01M7 16.5h.01"/>
areas.lead: Chat, voice and the wake word stay loaded. A picture, video or music job waits in line, or is refused with a reason when memory is short.

visual.alt: Drawn illustration of job lines: chat and voice answer at once, a picture is running with one waiting, a film clip runs while another waits.

bullets: Chat, voice and the wake word stay loaded, so a long film does not push them out
Heavy jobs wait in line, one at a time, in the order they arrived, and each shows its place in line
A smaller job that fits can go ahead of a bigger one that is waiting, but a waiting job is never passed for more than 10 minutes
When a job cannot run, you get a reason in plain words

areas.name: Health and logs
areas.card: See what is wrong and fix it.
areas.lead: Every problem is listed in plain words with one fix, and recent engine log lines are on one screen.

visual.alt: The Health page: two problems, each with a sentence about what is wrong and one button to fix it.

bullets: A short health list. Each item says what is wrong and offers one fix button
Recent log lines for each engine, with secrets removed, on the Engines screen
The Helper reads the same health and logs, so you can ask about them

areas.name: The Helper
areas.lead: A small built-in assistant on the admin page that answers questions about your setup.

visual.alt: The Helper screen: a short conversation ending in a card with Confirm and Cancel buttons before a restart.

bullets: Ask in plain words, like "Is everything healthy?" or "How much memory is free?"
It reads health, features, models, memory, logs, settings and updates on its own
It asks before it changes anything: a Confirm and Cancel card, and nothing changes until you confirm
It has its own small model, so it works even when chat is broken, and your questions stay on your computer

areas.name: Connect your apps
areas.lead: Chat, speech, pictures and more answer on one local address in the OpenAI format. Stack picks the engine.

visual.alt: Drawn illustration of a request to the local chat address and the reply headers that name the engine and model.

bullets: Each job is a role on a standard path, such as chat completions, embeddings, transcription, speech and images
Every reply says which engine and model answered, in a header
API changes are additive, and the OpenAPI description is generated from the code
Today every write needs Home's token header. Optional keys for other apps are planned, not built (status: Planned)

areas.name: Updates and rollback
areas.card: Stay current, and go back if needed.
areas.lead: Update an engine, and go back if the new one misbehaves.

visual.alt: The Updates page: each engine with its installed and newest version, and an Update button when one is available.

bullets: Updates are checked only when you click Check now, or if you switch the check on
After an engine update the old build is kept, and a Go back button returns to it
If a new engine build does not answer, Stack keeps the old one
Stack itself updates from a checked release and goes back to the old build on its own if the new one does not answer in about 30 seconds
An update never touches your data
